The Guun were an old race, older than history. It was probably their age, accompanied by awe-inspiring technology, that garnered the great respect afforded to the Guun by the other space-faring peoples. The Guun were the undisputed masters of the galaxy and EVERYONE acknowledged it.

Giinuu, Third Spawn of the Fifth House of the High Court of The Exalted Sixteenth Emperor, was a Guun Diplomat. This was a great honor, as only the most intelligent and capable sentients could be trusted to adequately represent the Honor and Glory of the Empire to the lesser races. On this day, a curious Giinuu was waiting to speak with the representative of a new space-faring race from a small world in one of the outer galactic spiral arms.

These meetings were fairly uncommon. Only a few races ever made it to the stars. Fewer than one a galactic cycle. To meet with their representatives, to bring them into the Empire, to fit them into the great pyramid of imperial privilege and responsibility, was a great honor. Where would these Humans fit in, Giinuu wondered.

An attending Genemeld alerted Giinuu to the arrival of the Human Diplomat. Giinuu pulled himself to his full height and stood regally, looking to make a good first impression. His blue-gray skin was polished to gleaming. His four eyes were a solid deep violet, the mark of Noble Blood. Yes, the young sentient wouldn't be able to help being awe-struck at the sight.

Soon, the airlock opened and a small group of six sentients entered. They REALLY were a small group, less than half of Giinuu's impressive height, and stocky to boot. Their arms swung back and forth as they walked, and they moved their heads around to view their surroundings. They looked utterly unevolved. "Looks like another worker race." Giinuu thought rather charitably. After all, better workers than eradicated.

The humans stopped a few paces from Giinuu. Two of them had lighter colored fur and eyes. The other four were darker complected and larger. Obviously servants of some sort. Giinuu was glad, at least, that these creatures hadn't attempted to bring any fighters with them. It would have been difficult to explain the need to kill such creatures at the outset of such talks.

"I am Robert Conner, representative of the Solar Confederacy, and I am here to speak on behalf of Humanity."

The creature DARED speak before a Guun Noble? Didn't it see Giinuu's height? Didn't it see Giinuu's eyes? Was it so very stupid that it couldn't see that Giinuu was a superior being? Giinuu controlled himself, as only a Guun Noble could, and spoke patiently.

"I am Giinuu, Third Spawn of the Fifth House of the High Court of The Exalted Sixteenth Emperor. I will accept your submission on behalf of your people."

The humans looked back and forth at each other in seeming confusion before answering; yet ANOTHER insult.

"I'm sorry, I don't understand. Submission? We are not here to submit to anyone. We are here to establish formal contact with your people, and ask about the possibility of opening trade negotiations. Did our translators get something wrong when they spoke with your people?"

Now, it was Giinuu who felt confused. Trade negotiations? My people? No Guun had EVER operated a communications outpost. Obviously these humans were simply too primitive to understand. He decided to explain as he would to a child.

"Who you spoke with before is unimportant. They would be a low race in honorable service to The Guun Empire, as are all races. You will serve as well. It is the way of things. Surely you understand now? So let us speak of important matters. The genetic collection ships will..."

"I'm sorry, I still don't understand. I can't speak on The Way of Things, but my people are neither prepared nor willing to submit to ANY outside authority. We are a Free people."

Free? Giinuu searched all through his translation implant, but could not find a solid translation of this strange word. The closest he could come is relief. Or maybe lacking? Were the humans saying they were unworthy to serve? Did they wish for eradication, instead? It HAD happened before, but was considered very dishonorable and wasteful. Giinuu wanted to prevent such a sad fate, so he decided to be soothing.

"Fear not, a great diversity of races serve The Guun Empire. All have their strengths and lackings. Your people will serve us well. Now, back to the genetic..."

"No. We will NOT serve."

The human interrupted Giinuu again, much to his consternation. The foolish creature was quickly turning this situation unsalvageable.

"Surely, you are NOT saying that your people would choose eradication?"

"We would, but you may not find it as easy as you think. I have come here peacefully, to make First Contact with an extra stellar race by my people. We would like to speak with you, learn from you, perhaps trade with you. We do not want trouble, we do not want war, but we will defend ourselves. Please, do not force us to do so."

Giinuu was stunned. What madness was this creature speaking? War? The last War was tens of galactic cycles ago. War no longer existed. Now, there was only The Guun Empire. There was only submission or eradication. Giinuu decided an object lesson was in order.

The Guun were an old race, and a powerful one. Billions of years of evolution had left them superbly adapted for rule. Their impressive height easily cowed many other creatures, their four large eyes could see both red AND green lightwaves, their light springy bodies were highly agile and they moved quickly by reflexively inflating and deflating their various fluid sacs. Most importantly, however, were their tentacles. Their twelve highly dexterous tentacles provided for both movement and manipulation. Furthermore, the tips of each tentacle were flexible enough to form shapes from suckers to stingers, and each was equipped with a small venom gland that was potent enough to leave most creatures writhing in pain for hours from one small sting. Giinuu was capable of striking fast enough with his tentacle to disable a Genemeld without even using his venom.

With the object of demonstrating that the Guun were capable of inflicting pain, Giinuu whipped his tentacle about and quickly stung the the human robertconner on an exposed paw. After all, almost no creature in the galaxy could resist a race that had advanced technology AND the capacity to inflict pain.

Robertconnor looked down at its paw and blinked. For a moment, Giinuu thought he might have been too forceful and broken the Human by accident, but then robertconnor abruptly spoke, in a strange tense tone.

"This meeting is over. If you want to speak again, message us by galactic transceiver. If we detect any ships bearing your peoples' spectral signature, they will be treated as hostile."

Giinuu was beyond confused. The human was angry. It wasn't awed, it wasn't adraid, it was ANGRY. What manner of creatures were these Humans? Obviously, they were more sturdy than they seemed. Giinuu was determined to show them The Way of Things. He struck again, at full speed, with his venom gland fully primed. He struck the Human robertconnor full in the cheek. It was a mistake.

His tentacle immediately exploded in agony as if he had just struck a stone. Three fluid sacs were obviously ruptured, judging by the dark viscous fluid now secreting from the discolored flesh of the tentacle tip. Obviously the Human had an internal skeletal structure, judging by its shape; but how hard must its bones be to withstand a blow like that?

Then, Giinuu was aware of a strange POP POP sound and felt as if he had just been struck in his main stalk by an out of control transport sled. Respiration was suddenly difficult, and he noticed a pool of circulatory and pressure fluids forming on the floor around him as his strength waned and he sunk to the ground.

Looking around, Giinuu saw that robertconnor had not moved. He stood impassively, before a scene of unbelievable violence. The second light-furred human stood close by holding an angled tube of metal pointed at Giinuu with a small stream of smoke wafting from the tip. A concealed personal sized weapon? Devious! The other, larger, four Humans were pointing similar pieces of metal at Giinuu's entourage of Genemelds and Trustees. The weapons again and again made POP POP POP sounds, accompanied by small flashes of light. Green and Yellow blood sprayed the walls of the meeting chamber and before any of the attendants could react, they were all dead.

Giinuu felt his own life beginning to fade as well. His body no longer had enough fluid to support itself, and he lay in a puddle of his own flesh and fluids. He watched the Humans quickly leave out the same airlock through which they had arrived, and wondered how it could have gone so wrong. He was a Guun, a Galactic Noble, one of the most highly evolved beings in Creation. How had he failed so thoroughly to subdue these animals?

And then Giinuu saw his mistake. As his purple eyes began to dim, Giinuu realized that the Humans were not mere animals. They were not simple workers. No, despite their unassuming looks, these humans were...

Without a doubt...

Predators.

"Mister President, we are nearing Alpha Draconis. Forward attack squadrons report the first ring of defensive fortifications have fallen and they are switching to secondary targets. Third, Fifth, Seventh, and Ninth Fleets beginning braking maneuvers. Forward cannons and lasers at the ready, mass drivers on standby."

Alpha Draconis. Primary system of the Guun Empire. Seat of their Throne World. After twenty years of all-out war, he had finally arrived. Robert Conner, Sixth President of the Solar Confederacy, had come to end the Guun War.

"Grand Admiral Erikson, signal the even-numbered Fleet Admirals to assume positions at their assigned positions. I want the outer and mid rims locked down tighter than a priest's collar before we move in-system."

Twenty years. That's how long it had been since that squid had slapped him. It hadn't hurt, of course. The squids themselves had no muscle, no bone, and were frail compared to humans. They were venomous, and Robert had been concerned for a moment when he first felt the sting in his hand. But the venom wasn't very potent, less than that of a honeybee, and his medical implants had quickly nullified its mild soporfic effect. To think that so many hundreds of millions of sentient life forms had died as a result of those pitiful slaps. It was insanity.

But these Guun were beyond insane. They were completely and utterly... Alien.

Shortly after President Conner returned to Sol after his disasterous First Contact with the Guun, it became apparent just how alien they were. Their Empire continued to communicate with the Confederacy by galactic transceiver, but there was some disconnect between the beings communicating and the Guun leadership. Communications between the Confederacy and the Guun Empire seemed to consist of nothing more than accusations of barbarity, invitations to join the Empire as some sort of worker caste, and repeated calls to submit to eradication. The dumb squids actually expected the humans to simply stand by and let themselves be enslaved or exterminated.

It nearly happened anyway.

Despite their physical frailty, the Guun Empire's technology was thousands of years beyond the humans'. This was demonstrated in the first battle of the war; The Fall of Titan. Four months after First Contact, the spectral signatures of two Guun ships were detected decelerating into the Sol system. Solar Fighters, century-old relics of the Second Colonial War, were dispatched from Titan, Europa, and Ganymede Colonies to intercept. It was a terrible defeat.

The three-kilometer wide alien ships were crystalline in structure, resembling giant snowflakes. Thirty-six Solar Fighters engaged two Guun Crystal Ships at the L4 Lagrange point between Saturn and Uranus and were completely destroyed. Their missile targeting systems couldn't even detect the enemy vessels, let alone lock on. And their onboard lasers were entirely ineffective. They may as well have been shining flashlights at them. The Guun responded with a focused gravity wave that decimated the attacking fighter craft. The few survivors were quickly picked off by coherent photon rays that put the Solar Fighters' ten megawatt lasers to shame.

The battle lasted less than fifteen minutes.

After the Solar Fighters had been dealt with, the two Guun ships advanced on Titan Colony. Titan was the smallest Human Colony, at only 30 Million People, and was the farthest from Earth. It never stood a chance. The last images sent back to the inner-rim by long-range satellites showed Titan Colony completely engulfed in the eerie blue light of a Guun gravity beam, disintegrating away to nothing.

And so it went for Five years.

Ganymede Colony fell a year after Titan, almost to the day. Despite a year's preparation, more Solar Fighters, stronger lasers, better sensors; the Fall of Ganymede was almost an exact repeat of Titan. In almost no time at all, another 50 million citizens were gone.

Europa fell one year after Ganymede, with one major difference. During the battle for Europa, one lone pilot in a vessel damaged by a coherent photon ray, launched a suicide attack on one of the enemy Crystal Ships and damaged it. Noticing that his fighter had drifted into a small blind spot in the enemy's field of fire, the Human Pilot, Peter R. McMurray didn't hesitate to kick his engines fully-open and ram them at mach 10. The resulting explosion blew several crystal spires off the primary structure, and damaged the main hull. The undamaged ship still completely obliterated Europa, and all 45 million of its colonists. But afterwards, the Guun didn't return to Sol for nearly two years.

The attack on Callisto was a surprise. The humans hadn't grown complacent, but their vigilance had waned so that after two years, they barely noticed the spectral signature of the four incoming Crystal Ships. They had spent the time examining data recorded during the previous battles, as well as the Crystal Fragments recovered from Europa. But the countermeasures being developed were not ready, and so Callisto was only slightly better defended than Ganymede. It fell in under an hour, and the Guun ships left the Solar System again.

They returned two weeks later to assault the colony on Io, almost as if they were making up for lost time. This time, they faced the largest sortie of Solar Fighters yet. Two Guun Crystal Ships faced off against One Hundred Twenty Three Solar Fighters over Io, with the lives of 70 million people in the balance.

The human ships swarmed like angry hornets. They quickly closed near enough that the Guun gravity wave attacks were useless; only ten or so fighters were lost that way. But the Guun photon rays were inhumanly fast and unerringly accurate, and the humans were mowed down like wheat. But they wouldn't stop. The Solar Fighters, no longer bothering with AI assisted targeting scanners, launched their missiles at point blank range.

Explosions as bright as suns blossomed on the main hulls of the Guun Crystal Ships. In one well-coordinated attack, over a dozen 50 megaton tactical nuclear warheads detonated almost simultaneously. The Guun ships' crystalline structures were mostly unaffected by the heat of the blasts, but the concussive force of the explosions left deep scores and large cracks in the hulls. Seizing the opportunity, those ships that were out of missiles and not yet destroyed, did their best to emulate the now famous Captain McMurray and launch their own kamikaze attacks on the damaged Guun ships. Again and again, nuclear missiles detonated and human pilots screamed defiance as they threw their lives at the alien invaders who had come to kill their families. And there, at Io, at a casualty rate of 123 to 1, the humans destroyed their first Guun ship.

Unfortunately, the remaining three Crystal Ships, though damaged, were still capable of firing their gravity beams at the Colony. And though it cost them this time, the Guun Empire claimed another 70 million human lives.

"Mister President." Robert Conner snapped out of his ruminations at being addressed. "Braking maneuvers completed. We are now In-System. Forward attack squadrons report secondary defensive positions have been destroyed and they are moving to fleet support positions. Third and Fifth Fleets moving to Outer Rim L2 and L3 Lagrange Points. Seventh and Ninth Fleets moving to Mid Rim L4 and L5 Lagrange Points. Even Numbered Fleets 2 through 10 moving to primary assault positions. Spectral Imaging shows Crystal Ships incoming."

"How many?"
